A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ProbeX and Model Jungle, with matching Sections 1–9 and Appendices A–H. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. The additional reference page in v3 shifts the appendices without removing material.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-tree experiments, classification, retrieval and out-of-distribution detection results, with additional ablations and model-population analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the classification comparisons in Tables 1–3 and the appendix ablations and retrieval examples.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same learned probes, shared projection, per-probe encoders, ReLU activation, prediction head and tree-routing procedure. Training objectives and inference procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same motivating CIFAR100 populations and Model-J coverage: four discriminative model trees and Stable Diffusion SD200/SD1k. Classification, zero-shot classification, retrieval and one-class detection scenarios are retained without additions.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their respective Random, StatNN variants, Dense and raw-weight comparators. Neural Graphs remains an unsuccessful attempted baseline described in Appendix H.2.1. The newly cited concurrent LoRA method is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix H retain the 70/10/20 split, 500-epoch per-layer training and validation-based layer/epoch selection. Dataset-generation settings, held-out classes, metrics and ablation protocols also match.

E4.justification: The tree-transfer experiments, activation and text-encoder ablations, dimension/depth/sample-size studies, layer analysis and retrieval examples are unchanged. Corresponding evidence remains in Figure 3, Tables 4–6 and Appendices B–E.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point estimates, class-averaged AUC reporting and model-population distributions. Neither adds an explicit repeated-run protocol, confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical tables, plotted results and qualitative examples match throughout both PDFs. For example, Table 2 retains ProbeX zero-shot accuracies of 0.898 on SD200 and 0.505 on SD1k; appendix layer rankings and ablation outcomes are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, Propositions 1–2 and their Appendix A proofs are unchanged. The expressivity argument and Tucker-decomposition derivation retain the same assumptions and equations.

C1.justification: The three stated contributions remain simpler learning within Model Trees, ProbeX and zero-shot classification through weight-language alignment. The revised model-search framing foregrounds applications already described in v2 Sections 6.1–6.2 without changing the claimed technical capabilities.

C2.justification: The explanations of nuisance variation, nonlinear generalization, layer behavior and overfitting are retained. Section 8 and the appendices preserve the same limitations concerning unseen trees, discriminative-model text alignment and deeper encoders.

D1.justification: Appendices C and F–H retain the same clustering details, hyperparameter ranges, optimizer settings, data-source information and baseline implementations. Reported hardware, training times and project/model-source links are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references covering interpretability, model search and model merging, and explicitly discusses Putterman et al.'s concurrent Learning on LoRAs as related to probing. This broadens the literature context while retaining the central single-hidden-layer probing distinction.

P1.justification: The abstract opening, introductory motivation and conclusion are revised to foreground missing documentation and model search. Related-work prose expands and an affiliation line is removed, while the section structure and most text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 receive revised captions, Figure 2 is slightly resized, and Tables 3–4 are rearranged on page 8. All figures and tables remain, with further page and column reflow caused by the textual and reference additions.

improvement.justification: v3 explains the practical model-search motivation more clearly and acknowledges relevant probing and concurrent LoRA work omitted from v2. These changes modestly improve context and attribution. The methods, empirical evidence, proofs, reproducibility information and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
